overview.title: A living Andalusian-Moroccan medina
overview.p1: Tetouan's medina is a UNESCO World Heritage site celebrated for its well-preserved Andalusian character. Whitewashed walls, narrow lanes, and a dense network of souks create one of Morocco's most atmospheric historic centres.
overview.p2: Unlike larger medinas, Tetouan's feels more residential and manageable. Artisan workshops for leather, textiles and metalwork remain active, and the gates open directly onto Place Hassan II and the Spanish Ensanche.
overview.p3: Allow two to three hours for a thorough walk. Mornings are cooler and quieter for photography and workshops; late afternoon brings warmer light and more local life.

q1.question: Is the Tetouan Medina free to visit?
q1.answer: Yes, walking through the streets and souks of the Medina is completely free and open to the public.

q2.question: What is the best time to visit the Tetouan Medina?
q2.answer: Mornings are quieter and cooler for exploring the artisan workshops. Late afternoon offers great lighting for photography against the white-washed walls.

q3.question: Is there a dress code?
q3.answer: As a traditional residential and commercial area, modest clothing covering shoulders and knees is recommended out of respect for local culture.

q4.question: How long does a tour of the Medina take?
q4.answer: A standard guided or self-guided walk takes about 2 to 3 hours to comfortably explore the main souks and gates.

q5.question: Can I visit without a guide?
q5.answer: Yes, many travelers explore independently, though a guide can enrich the experience by explaining the Andalusian history and heritage.
